sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Membrane localization confirmed by immunostaining; synaptogenic function explicitly stated to be maintained (HEK293 co-culture synaptogenesis assay, L8). In neurons, AP-NLGN1 rescued endogenous NLGN1 knockdown and displayed normal synaptic confinement by single-molecule tracking (L1/L2). KI mouse with bAP at this position showed surface biotinylation and streptavidin visualization of endogenous NLGN1 (L4/L5).
sites.rationale: Signal peptide spans residues 1–45 (authoritative landmarks); a tag upstream of residue 46 would be cleaved with the SP and silently lost. L8 explicitly states the HA tag follows the signal sequence, placing it at the unique extracellular N-terminus (insert_after_residue=45, residue_before=S, residue_after=Q). Python confirms residue 45=S and residue 46=Q. The mature ectodomain is 670 residues long, so the junction is far from the TM boundary (≥3 residues satisfied by a wide margin). L4/L5 independently confirm 'inserted after the signal peptide' in a knock-in mouse, and L1–L3 confirm N-terminal AP/bAP tags on full-length NLGN1 in neurons, all consistent with this single extracellular terminus. HA tag inserted following the signal sequence of full-length NLGN1 (B splice variant) expressed in HEK293 cells; signal sequence spans residues 1–45 by authoritative landmarks, placing the tag at the unique extracellular N-terminus (residue 46). Multiple independent studies (L1–L8) converge on this same N-terminal position using AP/bAP or HA tags on full-length, membrane-anchored NLGN1 in neurons and HEK293 cells.

sources.claim: Specifically, we used the B splice variant of NLGN1, which has been shown to preferentially induce excitatory synaptic sites but can also induce inhibitory synapses. 34 Additionally, we included a hemagglutinin (HA)-tag following the signal sequence to enable immunostaining of NLGN1-overexpressing HEK293 cells while maintaining membrane localization and synaptogenic function of the protein.

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines supporting extracellular tags on NLGN1 (L1–L8) converge on the same N-terminal position after the signal peptide (insert_after_residue=45). No paper names a specific residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived: with SP=1–45 there is exactly one extracellular N-terminus. L8 is chosen as the primary supporting clip because it is the most explicit about position ('following the signal sequence') and explicitly reports function preserved (synaptogenic activity). L4/L5 provide independent corroboration with the strongest biological context (endogenous knock-in mouse). L6/L7 (HA-Nlgn1 in neurons) are consistent but name no residue and are subsumed by the more explicit clips. The GFP insertion at position 728 (L9/L10) falls within the TM domain (716–738) and is described as 'below the transmembrane domain', placing it on the cytoplasmic face; it is recorded in other_positions as intracellular. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for NLGN1.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP inserted at position 728, which falls within the TM domain (716–738) and is described as 'below the transmembrane domain' (L10), placing it on the cytoplasmic/intracellular face; not a surface tag site.
